ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Base Case for KernelSHAP Analysis
PROPOSAL: Prove the base case for non-asymptotic sample-complexity analysis of KernelSHAP, which requires establishing a lower bound on the number of value-function evaluations needed to obtain an unbiased estimator of the Shapley values. Specifically, we will show that $2^{d-1}$ value-function evaluations are sufficient to achieve $\epsilon$-accuracy in the Shapley values.
CONTROLS: None
COST:  5000 
PREDICTION: Successful in establishing a base case for our analysis, with potential to trickle down to more complicated cases, but might struggle with balancing the generality of results with the level of technical difficulty.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Analyzing Nyström Method for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Explore using the Nyström method to reduce the dimensionality of the regression problem in KernelSHAP, which can be used to obtain faster convergence in the non-asymptotic sample-complexity analysis. We will derive the convergence rates for the Nyström method and show how it can be applied to the constrained weighted least-squares problem in KernelSHAP.
CONTROLS: Base case analysis without Nyström method
COST:  9000 
PREDICTION: Should be successful in deriving the convergence rates and applying the Nyström method, but the actual performance gain in practice might be limited by the overhead of dimensionality reduction.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Asymptotic Convergence Analysis of LeverageSHAP
PROPOSAL: Provide an asymptotic convergence analysis for the LeverageSHAP estimator, focusing on the sampling distribution of the rows in the regression problem. We will derive the central limit theorem for the LeverageSHAP estimator under certain smoothness assumptions on the value function, and analyze the asymptotic variance of the estimator.
CONTROLS: None
COST:  11000 
PREDICTION: Should be successful in deriving the central limit theorem and asymptotic variance, and provide insights into the behavior of LeverageSHAP under large sample sizes, but the actual relevance to non-asymptotic sample complexity may be limited.

ACTION: REVISE 
TITLE: (revised title doesn't change, rest of proposal copy does not change) MCMC-based Sampling for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Develop a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method for sampling the rows in the regression problem of KernelSHAP. Specifically, we can design an MCMC algorithm that samples the rows according to a distribution that matches the kernel weights in KernelSHAP. This allows us to obtain an unbiased estimator of the Shapley values while reducing the variance compared to uniform sampling.
CONTROLS: Baseline: uniform sampling
COST:  13000 
PREDICTION: Should be successful in designing an MCMC algorithm for KernelSHAP, but the actual accuracy and efficiency of the method may depend on the choice of MCMC proposal distribution and other parameters.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Asymptotic Convergence Analysis of LeverageSHAP
PROPOSAL: Provide a more detailed analysis of the bias and variance tradeoff in LeverageSHAP, and derive a non-asymptotic bound on the expected square error of the LeverageSHAP estimator. This will allow us to better understand the behavior of LeverageSHAP under finite sample sizes and choose the optimal parameters for the method.
CONTROLS: Asymptotic convergence analysis without non-asymptotic bounds
COST:  13000 
PREDICTION: Should be successful in deriving the non-asymptotic bound, and provide insights into the performance of LeverageSHAP under finite sample sizes, but the actual applicability of the bound may depend on the specific choice of parameters and datasets.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Evaluation of SimSHAP on Real-World Datasets
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of SimSHAP on a set of real-world datasets from various domains, including image classification, natural language processing, and recommender systems. We will compare the Shapley values estimated by SimSHAP with the true Shapley values computed using exact methods, and analyze the accuracy and computational efficiency of SimSHAP on these datasets.
CONTROLS: Baseline: exact computation of Shapley values
COST:  18000 
PREDICTION: Should be successful in evaluating SimSHAP on real-world datasets, and provide insights into its performance and limitations, but the actual applicability of SimSHAP may depend on the specific choice of parameters and datasets.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Non-Uniform Sampling for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of non-uniform sampling schemes for the rows in the regression problem of KernelSHAP. Specifically, we will design and evaluate a variety of non-uniform sampling schemes that are designed to reduce the variance of the KernelSHAP estimator, while also reducing the computational cost of the method.
CONTROLS: Baseline: uniform sampling
COST:  20000 
PREDICTION: Should be successful in designing and evaluating non-uniform sampling schemes, and provide insights into their performance and limitations, but the actual applicability of these methods may depend on the specific choice of parameters and datasets.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Theoretical Guarantees for Paired Sampling
PROPOSAL: Provide theoretical guarantees for the paired sampling scheme in KernelSHAP. Specifically, we will derive a non-asymptotic bound on the expected square error of the paired sampling estimator, and analyze the tradeoff between the variance reduction and the computational cost of the method.
CONTROLS: Baseline: uniform sampling
COST:  22000 
PREDICTION: Should be successful in deriving the non-asymptotic bound and analyzing the tradeoff, and provide insights into the performance and limitations of paired sampling, but the actual applicability of these results may depend on the specific choice of parameters and datasets.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Experimental Comparison of KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP
PROPOSAL: Perform an experimental comparison of the KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP estimators on a variety of real-world datasets. We will evaluate the accuracy and computational efficiency of both methods, and analyze the tradeoff between their performance and the number of value-function evaluations required.
CONTROLS: Baselines: exact computation of Shapley values, uniform sampling
COST:  28000 
PREDICTION: Should be successful in comparing the performance of KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, and provide insights into their strengths and limitations, but the actual applicability of these results may depend on the specific choice of parameters and datasets.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Tightening the Bound for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Attempt to tighten the non-asymptotic bound on the expected square error of the KernelSHAP estimator, and analyze the impact of this improvement on the theoretical guarantees for KernelSHAP.
CONTROLS: Current non-asymptotic bound
COST:  30000 
PREDICTION: Should be challenging to tighten the bound significantly, as it already reflects a delicate balance between the complexity of the value function and the randomness of the sampling scheme, but achieving such an improvement would greatly enhance the theoretical foundations of KernelSHAP.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing a Multimodal Temporal Reasoning Model for Change Understanding and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: 
Investigate the effectiveness of a multimodal temporal reasoning model (MTRM) for SITS. MTRM will integrate visual, temporal, and spatial cues through a hierarchical transformer-based architecture. It will be pre-trained on a large corpus of satellite images with associated temporal metadata and finetuned on the 2021 Land Cover Classification Validation dataset and the Brazilian Amazonian deforestation dataset. The model's performance will be evaluated using a combination of metrics, including BLEU, ROUGE, and automated C-Caps evaluation for temporal consistency.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Static image captioning model (e.g. Vision-LM) on the same datasets.
- Baseline 2: State-of-the-art temporal change description models (e.g. TimeNet) without multimodal reasoning.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: This proposal has high potential as MTRM can capture both visual and temporal information, potentially improving understanding of past changes and temporal consistency of forecasts. However, its effectiveness may suffer from the quality of pre-training data and the difficulty of temporal reasoning in the target domain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Long-Range Temporal Modeling on Temporal Consistency
PROPOSAL: 
Extend the MTRM from Proposal 1 with a long-range temporal modeling (LRTM) component, which will encode trends and patterns in the sequence of satellite images using a variant of the Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) technique. This component will be integrated with the MTRM in a multi-task learning framework, where the model is trained to minimize a loss function that balances the accuracy of temporal change description and the temporal consistency of the forecast. Evaluate the impact of LRTM on temporal consistency using the same datasets and controls as Proposal 1.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: MTRM without LRTM (Proposal 1).
- Baseline 2: Current state-of-the-art temporal change description models with LRTM.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The addition of LRTM may significantly improve temporal consistency of forecasts, but may also increase computational complexity and reduce model agility due to overfitting on training data trends.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Role of Causal Reasoning in Temporal Change Description
PROPOSAL: 
Design a causal reasoning module based on a probabilistic graphical model (PGM) to capture the underlying causal relationships between events and changes in the satellite image sequence. This module will be integrated with the MTRM and LRTM components from Proposal 2 to provide a comprehensive understanding of the past changes and their causal drivers. Evaluate the impact of causal reasoning on the accuracy of temporal change description using a modified version of the ROGUE metric that incorporates causal plausibility.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: MTRM + LRTM (Proposal 2).
- Baseline 2: MTRM + LRTM without causal reasoning.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: Causal reasoning may improve the accuracy of temporal change description, but its effectiveness may depend on the quality of the causal graph and the availability of sufficient training data. Over-reliance on causal models may also lead to failures in complex and dynamic systems where causality is unclear.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Temporal Consistency of Forecasts using a Novel Metric
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a novel metric, TC-Score, to evaluate the temporal consistency of forecasts. TC-Score will combine spatial and temporal features from both the ground truth and the predicted images to quantify their similarity. Implement TC-Score as a control for all experiments in the set, including Proposal 1, 2, and 3. Evaluate the performance of the proposed models using TC-Score in addition to standard metrics.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Standard image-quality metrics (e.g. PSNR, SSIM) for temporal consistency evaluation.
- Baseline 2: Current state-of-the-art metrics for temporal consistency evaluation (e.g. C-Caps).
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The proposed TC-Score metric may provide a more comprehensive evaluation of temporal consistency, but its effectiveness may depend on the quality of the implementation and the specific use case. It may also add computational overhead to the evaluation process.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Long-Range Temporal Modeling on Temporal Consistency
PROPOSAL: 
Modify the LRTM component from Proposal 2 to incorporate a variant of the Segmental Trajectory Model (STM), which can better capture the irregularly sampled nature of satellite image sequences. The modified STM variant will be combined with the MTRM and causal reasoning module from Proposal 3. Evaluate the impact of this modification on the temporal consistency of forecasts using the TC-Score metric and standard metrics.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: MTRM + causal reasoning (Proposal 3) without LRTM or STM.
- Baseline 2: MTRM + STM without causal reasoning.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: The modified LRTM component may improve the temporal consistency of forecasts, especially in scenarios with irregular sampling. However, its effectiveness may depend on the quality of the STM variant and the availability of sufficient training data. The modified LRTM may also increase computational complexity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: 
Explore the potential of transfer learning for satellite image time series forecasting by adapting models trained on large, diverse satellite image datasets (e.g. Landsat, Sentinel-2) to specific regions or applications. Use the pre-trained models as a starting point for finetuning on smaller, region-specific datasets. Evaluate the transferability of pre-trained models across different regions, dataset sizes, and applications.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Training models from scratch on region-specific datasets.
- Baseline 2: Using pre-trained models without finetuning.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: Transfer learning may significantly improve forecasting performance, especially when region-specific data is limited. However, the transfer ability may depend on the quality of the pre-trained model, the similarity between the source and target domains, and the availability of finetuning data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Change Description using Human-Labeled Annotations
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a dataset of human-labeled temporal change descriptions for a diverse set of satellite image time series sequences. Use this dataset to fine-tune and evaluate the multimodal temporal reasoning models from Proposal 1, focusing on the quality and accuracy of the generated change descriptions. Evaluate the impact of human supervision on the performance of the models and compare with models trained on automatically generated captions.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Models trained on automatically generated captions.
- Baseline 2: Current state-of-the-art models for temporal change description.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: Human-labeled annotations may significantly improve the accuracy and quality of temporal change descriptions, but may also introduce bias and require significant human effort. The effectiveness of human supervision may depend on the quality of the annotations, the diversity of the dataset, and the choice of evaluation metrics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multitask Learning for Joint Change Understanding and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a multitask learning framework that jointly trains the multimodal temporal reasoning model (Proposal 1) for change understanding and the satellite image time series forecasting model for forecasting. Use a shared encoder-decoder architecture that learns to jointly capture both the past and future changes in the satellite image time series. Evaluate the performance of the multitask model on both change understanding and forecasting tasks.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Separate models for change understanding and forecasting (Proposal 1 and 5).
- Baseline 2: Current state-of-the-art models for joint change understanding and forecasting.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: Jointly learning both tasks may improve the performance of both change understanding and forecasting, especially when the tasks are highly correlated. However, the effectiveness may depend on the choice of the multitask learning framework, the architecture of the shared encoder-decoder, and the availability of labeled data for both tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty Estimation for Change Understanding and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a framework for uncertainty estimation for both change understanding and forecasting tasks using advanced statistical techniques such as Bayesian neural networks and Dempster-Shafer theory. Evaluate the performance of the uncertainty estimation framework using metrics such as the mean absolute error and the mean squared error. Compare the performance of the uncertainty estimation framework with the baseline models from proposal 1 to 7.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Current state-of-the-art models for change understanding and forecasting.
- Baseline 2: Models without uncertainty estimation.
COST: 12600
PREDICTION: Uncertainty estimation may significantly improve the robustness of both change understanding and forecasting models, especially when the data is noisy or uncertain. However, the effectiveness may depend on the choice of the uncertainty estimation framework, the availability of labeled data, and the complexity of the underlying relationships between variables.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large-Scale Experiments and Ensemble Methods for Robust Performance
PROPOSAL: 
Conduct large-scale experiments to evaluate the performance of the proposed models (Proposal 1-8) on a diverse set of satellite image time series datasets. Use ensemble methods such as bagging and boosting to combine the predictions of multiple models and improve the overall performance. Evaluate the robustness of the ensemble methods using metrics such as the mean absolute error and the mean squared error.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Current state-of-the-art models for change understanding and forecasting.
- Baseline 2: Ensemble methods without large-scale experiments.
COST: 15120
PREDICTION: Large-scale experiments and ensemble methods may significantly improve the robustness and accuracy of both change understanding and forecasting models. However, the effectiveness may depend on the choice of ensemble methods, the diversity of the datasets, and the availability of computational resources for large-scale experiments.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Comprehensive Evaluation of Online Time Series Forecasting Methods
PROPOSAL: compare the performance of popular online time series forecasting methods on several real-world datasets, including traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, and weather forecasting. Evaluate methods using mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE).
CONTROLS: use baseline methods such as Naive Decay, Naive Approach, and seasonal decomposition with trend.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: This experiment will reveal which online time series forecasting methods perform best overall and on specific benchmarks, where things might fail is the potential overfitting to certain problem domains.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Adapter Modules on Online Forecasting Performance
PROPOSAL: evaluate the performance of online time series forecasting methods with different types of adapter modules (e.g., simple multilayer perceptrons, convolutional neural network adapters) on traffic flow forecasting and electricity consumption forecasting datasets. Compare the performance using MAE, MSE, and MAPE.
CONTROLS: compare adapter module variants with and without frozen base model.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The results will show whether adapter modules improve online forecasting performance and which types of adapters perform best under which conditions; overfitting in specific domains could limit advancements.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Analyzing the Effects of Online Adaptation on Concept Drift
PROPOSAL: compare the performance of online time series forecasting methods with and without adaptive mechanisms on concept drift scenarios using simulated data that mimics real-world traffic flow and weather forecasting scenarios. Evaluate methods using AUROC and average rank.
CONTROLS: compare the performance of methods under different concept drift intensities and frequencies.
COST: 2500
PREDICTION: This experiment will reveal whether online adaptation mechanisms can mitigate the effects of concept drift and which methods are most effective in adaptive scenarios, where things might fail is the difficulty in simulating realistic drift scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Investigating the Relationship Between Online Model Updates and Distribution Statistics
PROPOSAL: analyze the relationship between online model updates and distribution statistics (e.g., mean, variance, skewness) using real-world datasets in traffic flow forecasting and electricity consumption forecasting. Investigate whether normalized data improves online forecasting performance and if updates based on distribution statistics outperform standard online gradient descent.
CONTROLS: compare the performance of methods using different normalization techniques and updating strategies.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The results will show whether incorporating distribution statistics into online updates can improve forecasting performance and whether normalization techniques enhance or diminish these effects, where things might fail is the potential for overfitting to specific distribution types.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Analyzing the Effects of Online Adaptation on Concept Drift
PROPOSAL: modify experiment 3 to use real-world datasets in traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, and weather forecasting to evaluate the impact of online adaptation on concept drift. Introduce concept drift through methodological adjustments, such as seasonal changes in historical data, to more realistically assess the robustness of online time series forecasting methods.
CONTROLS: compare the performance of methods under different concept drift scenarios and durations.
COST: 3500
PREDICTION: This revised experiment will provide a more realistic assessment of online adaptation in the presence of concept drift using real-world data, where things might fail is the potential for drift mechanisms to be too simplistic or not representative of real-world dynamics.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Delays in Feedback and Gradient Estimation: A Study on Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: investigate the effects of delayed feedback on multi-step forecasting performance using a real-world dataset in traffic flow forecasting. Evaluate the impact of delayed feedback on gradient estimation and its influence on model adaptation.
CONTROLS: compare the performance of gradient-based methods with and without feedback delay, using different feedback delay intervals.
COST: 4200
PREDICTION: This experiment will show whether and how delays in feedback impact multi-step forecasting performance and identify potential solutions to mitigate this effect, where things might fail is the difficulty in calibrating realistic feedback delay scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Autonomous Dynamic Regularization for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: develop and evaluate a novel approach to dynamic regularization for online time series forecasting, which adaptively adjusts the regularization strength based on the recent evolution of the target distribution. Evaluate the proposed method using real-world datasets in traffic flow forecasting, electricity consumption forecasting, and weather forecasting.
CONTROLS: compare the performance of the proposed approach with standard gradient descent and other dynamic regularization methods.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: This experiment will show whether adaptive regularization can improve the stability and accuracy of online time series forecasting methods and how it compares to existing approaches, where things might fail is the potential for over-regularization or under-regularization in specific scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Online Transfer Learning for Time Series Forecasting acrossRelatedDomains
PROPOSAL: explore the application of online transfer learning to time series forecasting across related domains, such as weather forecasting and traffic flow forecasting. Develop and evaluate a novel transfer learning approach that leverages shared knowledge between domains to improve forecasting accuracy.
CONTROLS: compare the performance of the proposed transfer learning method with standard online learning and multi-task learning approaches.
COST: 5500
PREDICTION: This experiment will show whether transfer learning can be effectively applied to online time series forecasting and identify the optimal transfer scenarios, where things might fail is the difficulty in selecting relevant domains for transfer and avoiding negative transfer.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of Dynamic Regret in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: provide a theoretical analysis of dynamic regret in online time series forecasting, focusing on the trade-off between exploration and exploitation in adapting to changing distributions. Derive bounds on the dynamic regret of online algorithms and investigate their implications for practical algorithm design.
CONTROLS: compare the theoretical bounds with existing online algorithms and explore the role of exploration-exploitation trade-offs in reducing dynamic regret.
COST: 6500
PREDICTION: This theoretical analysis will provide a deeper understanding of the fundamental limits of online time series forecasting and inform the design of more efficient algorithms, where things might fail is the difficulty in translating theoretical insights into practical improvements.

ACTION: ADD 9
TITLE: Real-World Deployment and Evaluation of Online Time Series Forecasting Methods
PROPOSAL: deploy and evaluate the most promising online time series forecasting methods from previous experiments in real-world settings, such as traffic management and energy consumption prediction systems. Conduct a comprehensive evaluation of these methods using real-world data and assess their performance, scalability, and robustness in practical applications.
CONTROLS: compare the performance of the deployed methods with existing baselines and evaluate their potential for real-world impact.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: This real-world deployment will demonstrate the practical applicability of online time series forecasting methods and provide valuable insights into their performance and limitations in real-world scenarios, where things might fail is the difficulty in scaling and maintaining the deployed systems.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploration of Lightweight Dense Text Retrievers for Enhancing Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Experimentally evaluate the performance of ColPali-based encoders paired with a lightweight dense text retriever (e.g., Anaconda) on visual document retrieval benchmarks (e.g., MS MARCO, QCPR). Compare with the ColPali-based encoder alone, and ablate the dense text retriever to understand its contribution.
CONTROLS: ColPali-based encoder without dense text retriever, BM25 with image encoding, baseline late-interaction multimodal retrievers (e.g., ColBERT)
COST: 3600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The lightweight dense text retriever may improve the trade-off between retrieval quality and online latency, and potentially offer a useful complementary signal to the vision-centric encoder. It might struggle to reach the performance of the baseline late-interaction retrievers, especially under low-latency conditions.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Exploration of Lightweight Dense Text Retrievers for Enhancing Vision-Centric Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: Replace Anaconda with AnSi, a more recent and efficient dense text retriever. Additionally, investigate the impact of different text encoding architectures (e.g., sentence-BERT, unsupervised text encoders) and image feature extractors (e.g., ResNet-101, Swin Transformer) on the performance of the hybrid system.
CONTROLS: Same as before
COST: 8400 GPU-hours (with new experiments on different text encoding architectures)
PREDICTION: The new experiments may reveal that AnSi outperforms Anaconda, offering a better compromise between quality and latency. The investigation of different text and image architectures could help identify the most suitable combination, but might also reveal limitations and challenges in integrating these components.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing an Architecture-Agnostic Representation Aggregation Framework for Hybrid Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Design and experimentally evaluate a novel framework for combining the query-document interactions of two heterogeneous retrievers, dubbed "Interaction Aggregator" (IA). IA would be implemented using a neural network, allowing it to generalize across various architectures and scales of representations.
CONTROLS: Ablation study to demonstrate the value of IA, ColPali-based encoder without interaction aggregation, baseline late-interaction multimodal retrievers
COST: 10800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: IA may enable the exploitation of rich interactions within the representation spaces of both retrievers, but might also introduce additional latency and training complexity.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Developing an Architecture-Agnostic Representation Aggregation Framework for Hybrid Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Instead of a neural network, implement IA using a linear combination of the query-document similarity scores from each retriever. This simplified approach would be more computationally efficient and less prone to overfitting, allowing for better handling of diverse architectures and scales.
CONTROLS: Same as before, with an additional experiment on the linear combination approach
COST: 7200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The linear combination approach might not fully exploit the rich interactions, but could still provide a useful approximation with reduced computational overhead and improved robustness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Reparameterization on the Interaction Aggregator
PROPOSAL: Experimentally analyze the effect of reparameterizing the query-document representations from each retriever (e.g., using cosine normalization or feature whitening) on the performance of IA and the overall hybrid system. This could help identify optimal pre-processing techniques for improving the compatibility and synergy between the two retrievers.
CONTROLS: Experiments with and without reparameterization, baseline late-interaction multimodal retrievers
COST: 14400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Reparameterization might enhance the interaction between the two retrievers, especially when the representations have differing scales or distributions. However, the optimal approach could depend on the specific architectures and data characteristics involved.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Reparameterization on the Interaction Aggregator
PROPOSAL: Examine the effect of different reparameterization techniques on the similarity scores from each retriever, including matrix cosine similarity, produit-mix, and reparameterizing only the input embeddings. Additionally, investigate the influence of reparameterization on the hyperparameters of IA.
CONTROLS: Experiments with various reparameterization techniques, baseline late-interaction multimodal retrievers
COST: 19800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The results might reveal that certain reparameterization techniques have a significant impact on the performance of IA, while others have little effect. The investigation of reparameterization effects on hyperparameters could also provide insights into how to optimize the performance of the hybrid system.

ACTION: ADD

PROPOSAL: Measure the online latency, memory usage, and indexing time complexity of the hybrid system in comparison to a ColPali-based encoder alone. Investigate the effect of varying interaction patterns, embedding dimensions, and representational complexities on the memory consumption and latency of the hybrid system.

PROPOSAL: Examine the effect of incorporating query-level features (e.g., click history, relevance labels) into the hybrid model. Investigate whether leveraging these features enhances the retrieval performance and whether certain features have a more significant impact than others.

TITLE: Comprehensive Performance Analysis and System Optimization for Hybrid Multimodal Retrieval
PROPOSAL: Combine the results from previous experiments to provide a comprehensive analysis of the hybrid system's performance. Identify key factors that influence the system's performance and develop optimization strategies to improve its efficiency and effectiveness.
CONTROLS: None
COST: 43200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This study will provide a conclusive assessment of the hybrid system's capabilities and limitations, and the analysis will reveal potential areas for further improvement through model refinement, hyperparameter tuning, or system redesign.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating pre-training objectives for coverage in diverse reasoning traces
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of various pre-training objectives on the coverage of diverse reasoning traces using the GLM benchmark on science question-answering. Specifically, we compare the performance of BERT, RoBERTa, and a variant of BERT with a KL-divergence objective that encourages the model to generate diverse outputs. We also examine the impact of temperature on the diversity of generated outputs. For controls, we use the standard pre-training objectives of BERT and RoBERTa, as well as a baseline with no pre-training objectives (i.e., initializing the model randomly).
CONTROLS: BERT, RoBERTa, random initialization
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Our results may show that the KL-divergence objective leads to better coverage of diverse reasoning traces, especially when combined with high temperatures. However, we may also observe that the improvement comes at the cost of accuracy, leading to a diversity-accuracy trade-off. Also, we might not see significant differences between BERT and RoBERTa, as both are based on similar architectures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the effect of diverse initializations on mode preservation during fine-tuning
PROPOSAL: We investigate whether initializing the model with diverse outputs from different teacher models improves the preservation of distinct reasoning modes during fine-tuning using the GLM benchmark on science question-answering and code generation tasks. Specifically, we compare the performance of models fine-tuned from a single teacher model, multiple teacher models, and a randomly initialized model. For controls, we use standard supervised fine-tuning and a baseline with no fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: Standard supervised fine-tuning, no fine-tuning
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Our results may show that initializing the model with diverse outputs from multiple teacher models leads to better preservation of distinct reasoning modes, especially for harder science questions and code generation tasks. However, we may also observe that the benefits come at the cost of increased training time and computational resources.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the impact of mode-aware fine-tuning objectives on accuracy and coverage
PROPOSAL: We propose and investigate two mode-aware fine-tuning objectives: a softmax-based objective that encourages the model to assign higher probabilities to distinct reasoning modes, and a binary cross-entropy-based objective that penalizes the model for collapsing modes. We compare the performance of models fine-tuned using these objectives, standard supervised fine-tuning, and a baseline with no fine-tuning on science question-answering and code generation tasks. For controls, we use the GLM benchmark and evaluate models on both accuracy and coverage metrics.

TITLE: Nonlinear Attention Mixture with Element-Wise Operations
PROPOSAL: Design an attention mechanism that replaces the linear mixing in existing sequence mixers with element-wise nonlinear combinations of the key-value pairs, enabling per-channel, context-dependent selection. Specifically, define $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ as a fixed element-wise nonlinear activation function, such as ReLU or sigmoid. The step-$t$ read is then given by $o_t = \sum_{i\le t} f(\alpha_{t,i} v_i)$, where $\alpha_{t,i}$ are the softmax attention weights. To maintain causal parallelism, compute the element-wise products $\alpha_{t,i} v_i \in \mathbb{R}^d$ in parallel using a fixed tensor with the softmax attention weights $\alpha_{t,\cdot}$ and the values $v_i$ as inputs. Finally, apply $f$ element-wise to the results to obtain the read $o_t$.

PREDICTION: The nonlinear attention mixture model should demonstrate improved expressiveness for tasks where channel-wise structure is critical, such as multivariate time series modeling, while maintaining competitive performance on simpler sequence modeling tasks. TITLE: Channel-Dependent Selection using Quantized Attention
PROPOSAL: Modify the standard masked softmax attention mechanism to support channel-dependent selection by introducing a learnable scalar quantization factor for each channel. Specifically, define $q_t^{(j)} \leftarrow q_t^{(j)} \cdot \exp(\beta^{(j)})$ and $k_i^{(j)} \leftarrow k_i^{(j)} \cdot \exp(-\beta^{(j)})$, where $\beta^{(j)}$ is a learnable scalar parameter for channel $j$. This contravenes modularity, hence  introduce adjustment terms $s_{t,i}^{(j)} = \beta^{(j)} + q_t^{(j)} k_i^{(j)}/\sqrt{d}$ in place of the original hidden term $q_t^\top k_i/\sqrt{d}$. Then set $\alpha_{t,\cdot}^{(j)}=\mathrm{softmax}(s_{t,\cdot}^{(j)})$ to set, for each head, a probability distribution over $\{1,\dots,t\}$. A separate vector, $\bm{\beta}$, maps model's depth to its channel: when processing the first layer this is equal to the same parameter from above, when processing the last layer equal to the same value for each $\beta^{(j)}$.
CONTROLS: Ablate the learnable scalar quantization factors to recover standard masked softmax attention.
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: Channel-dependent selection using quantized attention may improve sequence modeling performance, particularly on tasks with multivariate outputs.
